lessons.title: Planning a promotion
lessons.html:
What a promotion is for

A promotion is a short-term activity to increase sales or achieve another specific goal: clear slow or short-dated stock, launch a new product, attract new customers, build loyalty, or win back market share from a competitor. Examples in agri retail include a pre-planting fertiliser special, a "buy 10 bags of lick, get a free mineral block" deal, a winter feed demonstration day, or a supplier-sponsored animal health talk with discounts on the day.

Set a clear, measurable objective

"Sell more dewormer" is vague. "Increase dewormer sales by 25% compared with the same four weeks last year, at a GP% of at least 18%" can be measured. Set the objective before deciding on the mechanism.

Choosing the mechanism

MechanismBest forWatch out for
Price discountQuick volume, clearing stockEroding margin; customers waiting for specials
Bundle or multi-buyRaising basket sizeStock of both items must be sufficient
Free gift or sampleNew product trialCost of gift; supplier support
Competition or lucky drawFootfall, data collectionConsumer Protection Act rules for promotional competitions; POPIA for entries
Demonstration or farmers' dayTechnical products, relationshipsPlanning, safety and venue costs

Planning details

  • Timing: align with the farming calendar and avoid clashing with other promotions.
  • Stock: confirm quantities with buyers and suppliers in advance; running out mid-promotion damages credibility.
  • Pricing: load promotional prices in the system with exact start and end dates.
  • Budget: discounts, advertising, materials, staff overtime, catering. Negotiate supplier contributions.
  • Approvals: get management sign-off on the plan, budget and any legal wording.

lessons.title: Running the promotion
lessons.html:
Before launch

  1. Brief staff. Everyone on the floor and at the till must know the offer, the rules, the dates and the products included. Give a one-page summary.
  2. Prepare stock. Receive and position promotional stock, with back-up stock accessible.
  3. Set up displays and signage. Signs must state the offer clearly, including any conditions such as "while stocks last" or "limit 5 per customer". The displayed price must be the price charged.
  4. Test the till. Ring up a test transaction to confirm the promotional price or bundle discount applies correctly.
  5. Advertise. Use channels farmers actually see: WhatsApp broadcast groups, local radio, the co-op newsletter, flyers at the counter, notice boards at the auction pens, and social media.

During the promotion

  • Monitor sales and stock daily. Re-order early if stock is moving faster than planned.
  • Keep displays full, neat and safe.
  • Handle customer queries consistently; refer exceptions to the supervisor.
  • Watch for problems: till errors, misunderstandings, competitor responses.
  • Keep a log of issues and customer feedback.

Demonstration days

For a demonstration, such as a supplier showing a new knapsack sprayer or calibrating a planter, plan for safety. Keep the public at a safe distance from working equipment, never use real chemicals near spectators unless the event is planned and controlled by a qualified person, and have a first aid kit and first aider present.

Ethics and law

The Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008 requires that promotions are not misleading. Do not advertise a "special" that is not actually cheaper, hide important conditions, or run bait advertising where the advertised item is not reasonably available. Honour the promoted price for the advertised period.

lessons.title: Ending and evaluating
lessons.html:
Closing the promotion

  • Remove all promotional signage on the end date.
  • Confirm that system prices revert correctly; test at the till.
  • Return or reposition leftover promotional stock.
  • Collect supplier claims for agreed contributions, with sales data as proof.

Evaluating results

Compare results with the objective. Typical measures:

MeasureExample
Unit sales vs. same period last yearDewormer up 32% (target 25%)
GP% achieved19% (target 18%)
Total promotion costR14,000 incl. advertising and gift items
Incremental gross profitR22,500
New customers or accounts11 new accounts opened

Consider effects beyond the promotion: did sales of other products rise (halo effect), or did customers just buy earlier than they would have (pull-forward)? Did sales drop after the promotion?

Reporting

Write a short report: objective, what was done, results against target, costs, problems and recommendations. File it with the plan so the next promotion builds on what was learned.

Key points

  • Set a measurable objective before choosing the mechanism.
  • Confirm stock, prices, budget and approvals before launch.
  • Brief staff and test the till price.
  • Promotions must not be misleading under the Consumer Protection Act.
  • Evaluate against the objective and report lessons learned.
